executive_summary: This collection window (December 1-7, 2026) is the twenty-fourth archived window overall. Fresh search again re-checked both carried-forward CFDA institutional questions. The CFDA/Vogue Fashion Fund 2026 winner remains unconfirmed by any dated, sourced coverage from CFDA, Vogue, WWD, Business of Fashion, or Fashionista -- this is now the seventh consecutive window this signal has been carried forward open, roughly seven weeks after the October 20 gala; is_prolonged_silence('cfda-vogue-fashion-fund-2026-winner', all_reports) continues to return True. The CFDA Fashion Awards question was also re-checked, again finding no confirmed 2026 date, nominee list, or post-event coverage distinct from the Fashion Fund; this is the second window in which the question is tracked as a real signal_id (added last window), so is_prolonged_silence() correctly still returns False at two tracked entries against the four-window threshold, even though the underlying question has been informally described as open for roughly seven windows. This window's search also specifically looked for December-specific fashion-calendar activity: there is no December fashion week on the NYFW/LFW/MFW/PFW calendar (the next official NYFW window is February 2026 per CFDA's published schedule), and resort/cruise 2027 collections (Chanel in Biarritz, Louis Vuitton and Dior in the US, Gucci in New York) were confirmed to have shown in spring 2026, not in this window, so no new runway content originates here. One genuine in-window institutional/editorial event was found and is newly logged: Business of Fashion's annual VOICES gathering ran December 1-4, 2026 at Soho Farmhouse in Oxfordshire, UK, an invitation-only industry summit with more than 40 confirmed speakers including Kering's Luca de Meo, LVMH's Sidney Toledano, Levi's Michelle Gass, Tapestry's Joanne Crevoiserat, and Saks Global's Geoffroy van Raemdonck. This is dated, corroborated industry-leadership discourse squarely inside the window, but it is executive/business commentary, not garment, silhouette, or aesthetic discourse, and BoF's own event coverage is the corroborating source, which this report notes as a single-sector limitation. General winter-2026 coat-trend roundups (funnel necks, scarf coats, animal print) were found via editorial search but excluded as undated evergreen retail-editorial content rather than in-window reporting, consistent with this archive's prior handling of generic seasonal trend copy. No other in-window garment, silhouette, or aesthetic discourse independently verifiable to this window was found. On balance this window remains thin: two carried-forward institutional questions (one now formally past this archive's prolonged-silence threshold, the other in its second tracked window) plus one genuinely new but narrowly business-focused institutional/editorial event, no verified in-window style/garment discourse.

top_signals.name: CFDA/Vogue Fashion Fund 2026 winner still unconfirmed (seventh consecutive window; past this archive's prolonged-silence threshold)
top_signals.evidence: The CFDA/Vogue Fashion Fund's 2026 winner gala was held October 20, 2026. As of this window's search (covering Dec 1-7, roughly seven weeks after the gala), still no dated post-gala reporting naming a winner has surfaced from CFDA.com, Vogue, WWD, Business of Fashion, or Fashionista. The most recent dated coverage available remains the June 2026 finalist announcement (ten designers: Aisling Camps, Amir Taghi, Terrence Zhou/Bad Binch TONGTONG, Emily Dawn Long, Jamie Haller, Julia Ferentinos/Juju Vera, Zane Li/Lii, George Inaki/Milamore, Claire Sullivan, Zoe Gustavia Anna Whalen), plus the previously-noted detail that Anna Wintour did not sit on this cycle's Selection Committee for the first time.

top_signals.human_editor_note: Seven consecutive windows with zero indexed coverage of a named CFDA/Vogue Fashion Fund winner is well past ordinary reporting lag for a program this well-covered in prior cycles. This report does not speculate about a cause -- no winner name, delay, or cancellation is claimed or implied -- it states only that the silence continues and that this archive's own mechanism has flagged it as prolonged since the 2026-11-23 window. If dated coverage appears in a future window, reconcile and close this signal_id there with a real name and source; do not edit this or prior reports retroactively without new evidence.

top_signals.name: Business of Fashion VOICES 2026 industry gathering held in-window (Dec 1-4, Oxfordshire)
top_signals.evidence: Business of Fashion's annual VOICES gathering ran December 1-4, 2026 at Soho Farmhouse in Oxfordshire, UK -- an invitation-only summit with more than 40 confirmed speakers. Named participants include Kering CEO Luca de Meo, LVMH's Sidney Toledano, Levi's CEO Michelle Gass, Tapestry CEO Joanne Crevoiserat, and Saks Global CEO Geoffroy van Raemdonck, each in dedicated in-depth conversations. The event falls fully within this collection window.
top_signals.index_note: This is genuinely dated, in-window, corroborated industry-leadership content -- unlike this window's excluded generic winter-coat-trend roundups, which were undated evergreen editorial copy. It is flagged medium rather than high confidence because corroboration, while present across multiple BoF-owned event pages, does not yet extend to an independent outlet's coverage of the event's actual proceedings (as opposed to its schedule/speaker announcement), and because this is executive/business-strategy discourse, not garment or aesthetic discourse, which is the archive's primary interest per doc section 2.
top_signals.human_editor_note: Logged as a real, dated event rather than manufactured to fill this window's signal quota. It is deliberately not classified as style/garment discourse: BoF VOICES is a leadership and strategy convening, and this report does not stretch it into a claim about aesthetic trends. Saks Global's CEO appearing here is noted without further interpretation -- this report does not connect it to the company's earlier-2026 Chapter 11 restructuring beyond stating both are true; any such connection would be interpretation this archive doesn't have sourcing to support.
